title: The Evening Brief: Injuries reshape NFL, college football upsets reshape polls
dek: Monday evening brings a cascade of season-altering injuries across the NFL and college football, while early Week 2 results scramble the rankings and force teams to reshape rosters mid-stride.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The opening weeks of 2026 are inflicting irreversible damage: top-tier talent (Garrett, Aspinall, Pacheco, Davis) has left the field with surgery-requiring injuries, forcing contenders to pivot roster plans immediately rather than in December.
bottom_line: Week 1 and early Week 2 have imposed irreversible absences on contending teams: Garrett, Pacheco, Stribling, Davis, and Hand will miss months, forcing immediate roster surgery rather than year-end adjustments. Texas's comeback over Ohio State reset college football polls away from preseason consensus; the Longhorns now face immediate tests to hold the No. 1 ranking. Ballmer's reversal on fighting the Clippers sanctions and the Ravens' stalled extension talks with Jackson signal that institutional leverage shifts as the calendar moves forward. Watch Shelton-Zverev on September 15 and whether the American can break his 0-5 record against the top seed; monitor whether the injuries to Garrett, Pacheco, and others accelerate or stabilize through the next two weeks; and track whether Texas's ranking proves durable or transient once the team faces another power opponent.
body: The arc of Monday evening tilts sharply toward sudden absence. From the NFL to college football to professional tennis, institutions and teams are absorbing losses to injury and personal conduct that will echo through the season.

The NFL's injury toll is shaping up as the season's defining constraint. Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year acquired by the Rams in a blockbuster trade, underwent arthroscopic knee surgery on September 13 and will miss at least four games, eligible to return no earlier than Week 6 against Arizona. Isiah Pacheco, the Detroit Lions' planned backup running back, had back surgery on September 14 and faces a 12-week recovery, leaving the team to lean entirely on third-year back Jahmyr Gibbs through December. Tennessee tight end Ethan Davis, a key early-season target for five-star freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon, suffered a season-ending ACL injury Saturday against Georgia Tech. Falcons defensive lineman Da'Shawn Hand, signed as an offseason priority to bolster run defense, tore his quadriceps in Week 1 on just seven snaps and is seeking additional medical opinions before confirming season-ending surgery. The common thread: each injury struck a player expected to anchor his team's plan, forcing coaches to shuffle depth charts and cap strategies before Labor Day had passed.

College football's early rankings reshuffled sharply as well. Texas defeated No. 1 Ohio State 24-23 on Saturday with a 21-point fourth-quarter comeback, vaulting to No. 1 in the CBS Sports 138 rankings with 42 first-place votes in the Coaches Poll. Ohio State, which held 50 of 74 first-place votes before the game, dropped to No. 5. Oregon, which as recently as preseason held more first-place votes than any other team, fell to 1-1 after an upset loss to Oklahoma State at home and exited the top 10 for the first time since September 2023. The reversal highlights how sharply early-season results can reset polling once preseason reputation collides with Saturday tape.

Elsewhere, business and disciplinary moves sent their own signals. Steve Ballmer announced late Sunday he is accepting the NBA's sanctions against the Los Angeles Clippers, a one-year ban, $30 million fine, and loss of five first-round picks for salary-cap circumvention tied to Kawhi Leonard, after vowing to fight the ruling 11 days earlier. The reversal suggests federal exposure from the ongoing Department of Justice investigation trumped Ballmer's appetite for a public fight with the league. Baltimore Ravens owner Steve Bisciotti's public commitment to make Lamar Jackson the highest-paid QB in history has stalled: Jackson and the Ravens have not engaged in substantive extension discussions, per ESPN sources, with talks now tabled until season's end. The Ravens face a critical decision point: if Jackson remains reluctant after the playoffs, the team will have spent the entire 2026 season foregoing cap flexibility while watching its 2027 hole deepen. West Virginia assistant running backs coach Noel Devine, a former program star, was arrested Sunday on a felony strangulation charge with a preliminary hearing set for September 23; head coach Rich Rodriguez placed him on indefinite leave pending investigation.

On the court, Elena Rybakina captured the US Open women's title on September 12, defeating Aryna Sabalenka 6-4, 5-7, 6-2, and claimed the world No. 1 ranking. The victory leaves her one French Open title away from a career Grand Slam. The ongoing questions about her coach Stefano Vukov's methods, he was reinstated on appeal in August 2025 after a provisional suspension over findings of abusive conduct, remain unresolved even as she reaches the sport's top ranking. In the men's draw, Ben Shelton advanced to the US Open final by defeating Frances Tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 on Friday and will face top seed Alexander Zverev on September 15. Shelton holds a 0-5 record against Zverev; a victory would end a 23-year American men's Grand Slam drought. Top tennis players agreed Monday to end their 18-month public campaign against Grand Slams over prize money after the creation of a Grand Slam Player Advisory Council, though the truce hinges on the council's ability to close the gap toward the players' 22% revenue target. USA women's basketball won their fifth consecutive FIBA World Cup gold on September 13, defeating France 97-79 in Berlin, with Breanna Stewart earning MVP honors.

UFC heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall vacated his title on September 14 after reinjuring his right eye during training. Aspinall has been sidelined since October 2025 when Ciryl Gane's eye pokes damaged his eyes; the champion has undergone multiple surgeries and infections related to that initial injury. The vacant belt now clears Gane's path to undisputed champion status.

The week's narrative arc is one of sudden constraint: injuries forcing pivot plans, upsets resetting hierarchies, and institutional decisions reshaping rosters and leadership before Week 2 is complete. The coming days will test whether teams and leagues can absorb these shocks or whether the cascade accelerates.
